political_impact.text: The reorganization drew little public notice and no recorded press reaction: it moved names and boundaries on ground already federal and released nothing to private use.
The Forest Service came out of the summer with a rationalized map of named, supervisor-sized forests, all changing over on July 1, 1908.
No per-forest acreages were published for the changeover; the Forester could show area changes only by states.
political_impact.source: Report of the Forester for 1909, pp. 4–5

legacy.text: The compact, individually named national forest remains the Forest Service's basic administrative unit.
On December 1, 1908 the Forest Service was decentralized into six staffed district headquarters by departmental action, not executive order; districts became regions in 1930.
legacy.source: Report of the Forester for 1909, p. 13; Manual of Procedure (Nov. 16, 1908)
